description: This file implements the LOBPCG (Locally Optimal Block Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient) method for eigenvalue problems, including autograd support, with classes and functions for eigenvalue computation, orthogonalization, and Rayleigh-Ritz procedures.

classes.name: LOBPCG
classes.description: Worker class implementing the LOBPCG eigenvalue algorithm with methods for iteration, orthogonalization, residual updates, and convergence checks.

classes.name: LOBPCGAutogradFunction
classes.description: Custom autograd Function enabling gradient computation for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors obtained via LOBPCG.

methods.name: lobpcg
methods.description: Main function to compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors using the LOBPCG method, supporting autograd and batching.

methods.name: _lobpcg
methods.description: Internal implementation of the eigenvalue solver, handling batching, parameter setup, and execution.

methods.name: update
methods.description: Performs an iteration step in the LOBPCG algorithm, updating eigenvector approximations and residuals.

methods.name: update_residual
methods.description: Updates the residual vector based on current eigenvector and eigenvalue estimates.

methods.name: update_converged_count
methods.description: Checks convergence of eigenpairs based on residuals and updates the count of converged eigenpairs.

methods.name: stop_iteration
methods.description: Determines whether the iteration should stop based on convergence, iteration count, or external stop signals.

methods.name: run
methods.description: Executes the iterative LOBPCG process until convergence or stopping criteria are met.

methods.name: _get_rayleigh_ritz_transform
methods.description: Computes the transformation matrix used in the Rayleigh-Ritz procedure for eigenvalue reduction.

methods.name: _get_svqb
methods.description: Performs B-orthonormalization of a basis U, with optional dropping of small contributions.

methods.name: _get_ortho
methods.description: Orthogonalizes basis U against another basis V with respect to the B-inner product.
